parsed.rationale: The pipeline reports a Jaccard similarity of 0.714 between `_DequeStorage._growIfNeeded` (line 334) and `_DequeStorage._shrinkIfNeeded` (line 354), both private methods on the same type in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Deque.swift` within the `Core` package. Their names reveal symmetric, inverse operations (grow vs. shrink), which is a classic pattern where ~71 % of the body is identical bookkeeping (bounds checking, buffer reallocation, element copying) and only the resize condition and target-capacity expression differ. Collapsing the shared skeleton into a single private helper reduces the maintenance surface: a bug in the reallocation logic currently must be fixed in two places. Because both methods are private and intra-file, the change carries zero API-surface risk.

specifics.proposed_action: Extract the shared structural skeleton of `_DequeStorage._growIfNeeded` (line 334) and `_DequeStorage._shrinkIfNeeded` (line 354) in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Deque.swift` into a private helper method — e.g., `_resizeIfNeeded(condition: (Int, Int) -> Bool, newCapacity: (Int) -> Int)` — and have both methods delegate to it, differing only in the predicate and capacity-calculation closure they pass. Both methods remain in place as thin wrappers, preserving their distinct call-site semantics (grow vs. shrink).
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Neither `generic-parameterization` nor `subclass-lift` fits because both methods already live on the same concrete class (`_DequeStorage`) in the same file; there is no type hierarchy and no separate type to parameterise over. `extract-to-common` does not apply because the duplication is intra-file, not cross-package. `default-implementation` does not apply because no protocol is involved. The most idiomatic Swift remedy for two near-duplicate private methods on the same type is a shared private helper that accepts the differing logic as closure parameters — a refactoring that has no exact match in the named categories.
